messages:
maria: CI microbench flagged a regression on PR #2109 — batch kernel selection path looks off. failing threshold: batch_latency_mean increased from 0.95ms -> 1.45ms (50%+). see snippet from job output below.

ci-bot: :rotating_light: perf-checker: job red on 2026-03-19T14:02Z. test=runtime/microbatch/batcher_latency. allowed_delta=0.10ms measured_delta=0.50ms. link: https://ci.redwood/tests/2109

liam: Can you paste the failing log lines? is this on a specific GPU type or across the matrix?

maria: pasted minimal excerpt:
```
--- baseline (main) ---
batcher_samples: 1000
seq_len=64, batch=16 -> mean=0.95ms
--- PR/branch 2109 ---
seq_len=64, batch=16 -> mean=1.45ms
stack: runtime/batcher/kernels: batcher->kernel-priority->fallback-path
config: BATCH_SAMPLER=adaptive, KERNEL_AUTOPICK=1
```

sasha: This PR touched the kernel-priority heuristics (commit c3f9a2e). suspect the priority score normalization change. I can try a quick bisect on the CI repro harness.

jamal: I ran a local binary on a nc-8g testbed, reproduced roughly +40% median. Attached a small profiler snippet:
```
# top flame samples (PR vs main)
PR: kernel_select_engine::score_update (34%)
Main: kernel_dispatch (12%)
```

liam: If kernel_select_engine is taking 34% that matches a missed fast-path selection. Could be extra memcpy or a worse comparator. Try running the unit microbench with env DUMP_KERNEL_STATS=1 to get per-candidate costs.

maria: Ran with DUMP_KERNEL_STATS=1 — output:
```
candidate A: est_cost=0.98, measured=0.92
candidate B: est_cost=0.45, measured=0.44
selected: B on main
selected: A on PR (estimator overweights seq_penalty)
```

sasha: OK that points to the estimator tweak in c3f9a2e. I'll bisect within that commit. If we flip the normalization back it should revert selection.

ci-bot: bisect job queued by sasha; job id 5772. expected turnaround ~20m.

(devops-bot): Started ephemeral CI worker -> gpu: a100-40gb, image=prod-perf:v3.

jamal: quick note — this regression shows up only when batcher uses adaptive sampler (heavy variance). Static batching tests look fine. so rollout risk depends on traffic mix.

sasha: bisect result: commit c3f9a2e10 -> regression introduced in change to normalization factor. reverting the normalization line returns perf to baseline.

liam: Thanks. we should either revert the normalization or patch estimator to include an early exit for low-variance cases. Revert PR would be fastest for rollback.

maria: I'll open revert PR now and mark it as rollback-needed for the merge window. also adding a hotfix test to assert selection parity for seq_len=64/batch=16.

sasha: opened PR #2131 revert(c3f9a2e) and linked the CI job. requesting liam review.

liam: Reviewing now. If CI passes with revert, we should block the original merge until estimator is adjusted and tested.

ci-bot: PR #2131: perf-checker results -> all green. microbench delta within threshold.

maria: Reverted in prod branch, rolling out canary. rolling policy -> 5% -> 50% -> 100%. tagging oncall.

devops-bot: Canary rollout started. monitor: dashboard/runtime/batcher/latency.

maria: thanks all — follow-up action: create a unit that fuzzes sampler variance and asserts kernel selection invariants. tagging @sasha @jamal to own the test.

liam: Agreed. Also add a short note in the changelog about estimator heuristics to avoid re-introducing without perf evidence. :white_check_mark:
